policy: research authoring index only; not runtime admission; final Wave-1500 consolidation required

waves.focus: 2026 scoping review mapped 22 trials of supplemental glycine/collagen; all three glycine sleep trials reported at least one favorable sleep outcome, but collagen-to-glycine mediation has not been directly tested and efficacy evidence remains small/mechanistic.

Eight-week randomized placebo-controlled trial in 45 medication-naive children with ADHD/subthreshold symptoms; the higher-dose phosphatidylserine plus DHA arm improved selected attention, impulsivity, hyperactivity, reaction-time and Stroop outcomes, but DHA/formulation and pediatric-context boundaries prevent phosphatidylserine-only attribution.

Four-arm randomized triple-masked trial in 97 professional male football players; taurine+caffeine+phosphatidylserine combinations improved selected cognitive, psychomotor, sprint and locomotor outcomes, but the multi-ingredient design prevents phosphatidylserine-specific attribution and fatigue-resistance change was not established from baseline.

2026 human-evidence review summarizes small cognition, stress/anxiety and sleep-quality signals from randomized evidence, often stronger with caffeine; dose-range summaries are study exposures rather than consumer dosing guidance and heterogeneity/interaction uncertainty remain.

Thirteen-RCT meta-analysis in 561 adults age 50+ found no additional benefit of HMB plus resistance training for fat mass, muscle mass or muscle strength; direct null counterweight to routine HMB adjunct claims in exercisable older adults.

Seven-RCT sarcopenia meta-analysis found strength-training plus supplementation improved several functional/body-composition outcomes overall, but subgroup benefit was clearer for whey protein than HMB; combined-intervention evidence cannot be assigned to HMB alone.

Nine-RCT/496-participant sarcopenia meta-analysis found low-to-very-low-certainty improvements in handgrip, gait speed and physical-performance measures when amino-acid-based supplements were added to resistance training, with no clear muscle-mass benefit and substantial intervention heterogeneity.

Systematic review of recurrent-UTI prevention in women found therapy-specific differences: methenamine and vaginal estrogen had stronger support, while D-mannose and cranberry showed mixed efficacy; category evidence must not be collapsed into a generic supplement claim.

Sixteen-study/1,171-participant meta-analysis found no significant overall effect of fenugreek on ALT, AST or ALP; an ALP subgroup signal at higher studied exposures does not overturn the overall liver-enzyme null and is not dosing guidance.

Thirteen randomized placebo-controlled trials in adult men found a small total-testosterone signal but no stable free-testosterone benefit; all primary evidence was very low certainty and the authors rejected clinical/commercial testosterone-boosting claims.

Systematic review of six human studies found cautiously positive adjunctive signals for pain/function/imaging after tendon or ligament injury/repair, but evidence was sparse, heterogeneous, low certainty and many oral interventions were multicomponent.

Seven-RCT/188-participant meta-analysis found lower advanced oxidation protein products after exercise but no significant changes in several other oxidative, inflammatory or muscle-injury biomarkers; broader physiological/performance benefit remains unconfirmed.

Twenty-four-RCT meta-analysis found lower creatine kinase and LDH with astaxanthin but no significant improvement in VO2max, time-trial performance or maximal workload/power; recovery-biomarker signals remain distinct from performance efficacy.

Twenty-two-RCT/822-participant review pooled Spirulina, Chlorella, brown-algal polysaccharides and astaxanthin; selected aerobic/recovery signals were species-, dose- and training-context dependent, so the evidence remains category-level rather than transferable across algae products.

Systematic review of 11 controlled trials across ADHD and adult mental disorders found heterogeneous, inconsistent cognitive effects; current evidence did not support citicoline or phosphatidylserine-containing compounds as established cognitive enhancers.

Eight-RCT meta-analysis found a small reduction in CRP with Spirulina but no significant TNF-alpha or IL-6 effect, with significant heterogeneity; this supports a narrow biomarker statement rather than a broad anti-inflammatory claim.

Eighteen-RCT/1,023-participant diabetes meta-analysis found improved insulin-resistance and selected inflammatory/oxidative biomarkers, while LDL cholesterol increased modestly; disease-specific surrogate outcomes and mixed lipid direction remain explicit.

Twelve-RCT/3,350-participant meta-analysis in healthy working adults found a small pooled improvement in subclinical depression/anxiety/stress symptoms and lower cortisol, with no CRP effect and insufficient sleep evidence; strain/dose/duration heterogeneity remains substantial.

Six-RCT/341-participant meta-analysis of probiotic monotherapy in unmedicated depression found a small symptom benefit, but sensitivity analysis excluding industry-funded/adjunctive-agent studies became nonsignificant; formulation and funding-bias boundaries are first-class.

Forty-one-RCT meta-analysis found a modest cortisol reduction with probiotics, but heterogeneity was extreme and GRADE certainty very low; subgroup strain patterns and exposure ranges are not optimization guidance.

Network meta-analysis of 38 RCTs in major depression found signals across microbiota-based therapies, prebiotics and probiotic categories, but certainty was low-to-moderate and network rankings do not establish superiority of a specific strain or product.

Ten-RCT/486-participant meta-analysis in depression found lower CRP and TNF-alpha with probiotic supplementation, borderline IL-1beta change, and null IL-6/IL-10; biomarker findings remain distinct from antidepressant efficacy and strain-specific attribution.

Twenty-three-RCT/1,005-participant meta-analysis in overweight/obesity found no significant effect on body weight, BMI, fat mass, body-fat percentage, fat-free mass, waist-hip ratio, adiponectin or leptin, with only waist circumference significantly reduced overall.

Umbrella review of 45 systematic reviews covering 129 associations found only four high-certainty positive associations, including waist circumference and selected lipid/BP outcomes in specific populations; most health claims remain lower-certainty and population-specific.

Twelve double-blind placebo-controlled exercise trials found no significant IL-6 or malondialdehyde effect and a CRP reduction based on only two small trials; overall recovery biomarker evidence was low-to-very-low certainty and hypothesis-generating.

Pooled meta-analysis of four randomized placebo-controlled dementia trials (488 patients) with prior cerebral infarction found statistically significant benefits for cognition, activities of daily living and global clinical impression with proprietary EGb 761; subgroup/proprietary-extract boundaries remain explicit.

Systematic review of seven rheumatic-disease studies found promising symptom/inflammatory signals in rheumatoid and osteoarthritis populations, but overall certainty was low to very low because of small samples, heterogeneous preparations and short follow-up.

Forty-one-RCT systematic review found pooled improvements in several glycemic, lipid, blood-pressure and inflammatory biomarkers, while multiple other outcomes were null; surrogate-endpoint and baseline-risk modifiers remain explicit.

Thirteen-trial type-2-diabetes meta-analysis found statistically significant fasting-glucose, HbA1c, systolic-BP, triglyceride and HDL changes, but HOMA-IR, diastolic BP, total cholesterol, LDL and BMI were null and effect magnitudes were often of limited clinical importance.

GRADE-based 12-RCT blood-pressure meta-analysis found modest SBP/DBP reductions with ginger but rated certainty low because of inconsistency, short duration and limited robustness; dose-response subgroup findings are study evidence rather than dosing guidance.

Network meta-analysis of randomized trials in healthy aging/MCI found domain-specific signals for several nutrient combinations and single nutrients, but rankings were sensitive to sample size/duration and the heterogeneous interventions prevent ingredient-level equivalence claims.

Cochrane review of 16 randomized trials (4,083 children) evaluated oral vitamin B12 for growth, development and cognition; outcomes varied by endpoint and trial context, requiring age, baseline-status, co-nutrient and duration boundaries rather than a universal pediatric cognition claim.

Thirty-one-RCT glycemic meta-analysis found no significant fasting-glucose reduction with melatonin, while HbA1c, fasting-insulin and HOMA-IR signals improved; fasting-glucose null and metabolic-population boundaries remain first-class.

Twelve-trial/1,977-participant cancer-fatigue meta-analysis found a pooled fatigue reduction but very low GRADE certainty and substantial heterogeneity; apparent exposure/duration patterns are not converted into consumer dosing guidance.

Five randomized trials (323 hemodialysis patients) found improved PSQI and selected sleep domains with melatonin; the disease-specific evidence remains limited in certainty and should not be generalized to primary insomnia.

Five RCTs/561 breast-cancer radiotherapy patients found less fatigue and improvements in cognitive/global-health measures, with several emotional, social, physical, gastrointestinal, pain and sleep domains null; small samples and heterogeneous regimens limit inference.

Seven randomized IBS trials (391 adults) found improvements in overall symptom severity, pain frequency and defecation frequency, while quality of life and global sleep quality were not significantly improved; short-term IBS-specific evidence only.

Systematic/ethnobotanical review found historical abortifacient claims vulnerable to citation distortion and available animal/human data did not establish significant teratogenic or abortifacient activity; absence of robust pregnancy-specific controlled evidence keeps reproductive-safety conclusions incomplete.

GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 34 RCTs/1,769 adults found improvements on self-reported BDI/BAI scores but no significant HDRS, HARS or POMS effects; high heterogeneity and discordance between self- and clinician-rated outcomes constrain broad antidepressant/anxiolytic claims.

Eight RCTs in adult male soccer players found inconsistent biomarker/functional recovery effects, with more favorable soreness/well-being trends in selected tart-cherry, beetroot and curcumin studies; certainty was low or very low and remains category-level.

Systematic review of 14 black-cohosh clinical-trial reports found wide variation in CONSORT herbal-intervention and harms-reporting quality; the review chiefly informs evidence quality and adverse-event reporting rather than establishing efficacy.

International Menopause Society evidence update reviewed 158 studies and found most complementary-therapy evidence low/very-low certainty, with moderate-certainty support for selected black-cohosh/CHM/acupuncture combinations and vitamin-D outcomes; broad category evidence only.

Thirty-RCT review of 19 non-soy herbal interventions found substantial heterogeneity; most studies reported some symptom improvement but black cohosh and dong quai trials included null findings, preventing a class-wide efficacy conclusion.

Updated meta-analysis of 108 RCTs/7,137 adults found modest pooled improvements across several lipid, glycemic, blood-pressure, inflammatory and oxidative biomarkers, while ApoA1/ApoB, ALT, IL-6, BMI, weight and adiponectin were null; surrogate-outcome boundaries retained.

2026 retraction notice for a prior aged-garlic-extract blood-pressure meta-analysis; downstream evidence systems must quarantine the retracted synthesis and preserve retraction provenance rather than continuing to cite its pooled estimate.

Seven-RCT review of vitamin D and vitamins C/E in endometriosis reported selected pain/oxidative-stress signals but no significant pregnancy-rate improvement; multiple vitamins and heterogeneous regimens make this category-level adjunctive evidence.

Twelve-RCT MASLD meta-analysis found a triglyceride reduction with vitamin E but no significant overall total-cholesterol, LDL, HDL or BMI change; disease-specific lipid evidence is mixed and largely surrogate.

Systematic review of nine pediatric dialysis studies (194 patients) found limited, outcome-specific signals for hemoglobin/ESA use and cardiac function, with several lipid/inflammatory/QoL outcomes null; small heterogeneous evidence base limits pediatric inference.

Systematic review across mechanistic and clinical CAD evidence reported possible inflammatory/oxidative and selected clinical signals, but heart-failure and reinfarction results were inconsistent; mixed study designs prevent a high-certainty treatment claim.

Systematic review of clinical and experimental poisoning evidence found toxin-specific, mostly adjunctive signals for L-carnitine/acetyl-L-carnitine, with no basis to replace established antidotes/supportive care; heterogeneous toxins and mixed human/preclinical evidence require category-level handling.

New Zealand general-population analysis found substantial concurrent natural-health-product and medicine use, including potential interactions involving fish oil, coenzyme Q10, turmeric and glucosamine; one fish-oil/warfarin combination was rated potentially significant, and coding of supplement exposures was often incomplete.

Systematic review of melatonin use in children age 0-6 found rising prescribing, extended use and overdose exposures; short trials in neurologic conditions suggested sleep-onset benefit with few adverse events, but long-term outcomes and efficacy in typically developing young children were absent.

Umbrella review covering 52 reviews, 250 RCTs and 18 supplements found most evidence low/critically-low quality, with only selected moderate-certainty supportive-care benefits and dose-related or serious adverse events for some vitamins/minerals; broad category evidence only.

Twenty-study/1,737-participant GDM meta-analysis found improvements in glycemic markers and several pregnancy/neonatal outcomes with vitamin D, but substantial heterogeneity and methodological limitations make these exploratory disease-specific findings.

Pulmonary-tuberculosis meta-analysis found higher sputum-smear conversion and fewer adverse events with adjunctive vitamin D but no significant culture-conversion benefit; outcome-specific certainty and route/duration heterogeneity prevent a broad TB-treatment claim.

Critical ASD review found inconsistent observational status data and mixed RCT results; only one high-dose trial showed broad symptom improvements while other trials were marginal/null, leading the authors to reject vitamin D as a general ASD-targeted intervention.

Umbrella review of 21 asthma syntheses found a possible exacerbation-risk reduction with vitamin D but inconsistent effects on symptom control, lung function and inflammatory outcomes; evidence certainty was frequently low/very low and primary-study overlap was substantial.

Eight-RCT/617-participant hemodialysis meta-analysis found lower CRP and iPTH and slightly higher albumin with nutritional vitamin D, with no significant increase in overall adverse reactions, hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia; dialysis-specific evidence only.

Systematic review of 11 high-dose vitamin-D RCTs in multiple sclerosis found serum-level and immunologic changes with rare transient calcium disturbances, but clinical and MRI benefits were inconsistent; high-dose safety conclusions require monitored trial context.

Umbrella review of nine tuberculosis systematic reviews found consistently null primary outcomes for culture conversion, time to conversion and mortality, with subgroup signals considered hypothesis-generating; strong counterweight to routine adjunctive vitamin-D claims in unselected TB.

Umbrella review in diabetic kidney disease found low-certainty reductions in surrogate urinary albumin/protein markers but no consistent benefit for eGFR, creatinine, kidney replacement therapy, mortality or cardiovascular events, with safety inadequately reported.

Systematic review of 10 prospective breast-cancer chemotherapy trials found inconsistent efficacy across DHA/EPA combinations with or without vitamin D/GLA, no consistent treatment-response or survival benefit, and low-to-very-low certainty; co-supplementation prevents ingredient-level attribution.

Structured sports-nutrition review identified highest contamination/ADRV risk in multi-ingredient pre-workouts, weight-loss, muscle-building and testosterone-boosting products and emphasized third-party certification, product verification and documentation; product-quality/safety infrastructure evidence only.

Five-year randomized Finnish trial in 2,495 largely vitamin-D-sufficient older adults found neither 1,600 nor 3,200 IU/day reduced fracture risk; the lower-dose arm had more fractures than placebo, directly arguing against high-dose fracture-prevention claims in replete populations.

Fourteen-study hemodialysis meta-analysis found modest hemoglobin/TSAT improvements and lower weight-adjusted ESA requirements with ascorbic acid, but certainty was low, heterogeneity high, and long-term safety/patient-centered outcomes unestablished.

Systematic review of nutritional antioxidants in breast cancer highlighted a double-edged interaction with therapy: selected supplements may reduce toxicities, while antioxidant use during oxidative cytotoxic treatment may theoretically or observationally compromise treatment effects; broad mechanistic/clinical category evidence.

Forensic systematic review/meta-analysis linked supplement contamination to a meaningful share of unintentional anti-doping violations and described cardiovascular risks from performance-enhancing substances; contamination estimates and nutrition alternatives remain sport-regulatory context rather than product efficacy evidence.

Systematic review of 44 empirical studies estimated roughly 9-15% of tested supplements contained prohibited or undeclared pharmacological substances, especially stimulants/anabolic agents in pre-workout, weight-loss and muscle-building products; product-integrity safety evidence only.

Systematic review of five adolescent/youth creatine studies found no consistent short-term renal, hepatic or cardiometabolic safety signals or serious attributed adverse events, but the evidence base was small and lacked long standardized follow-up.

Meta-analysis of 48 athlete studies found higher odds of headache, abdominal discomfort, tachycardia, insomnia, anxiety, nervousness and increased urination with acute caffeine, with several side effects increasing with dose; safety effects remain distinct from ergogenic benefit.

Systematic review/meta-analysis in adolescent athletes found only a small uncertain acute physical-performance benefit, sparse cognitive evidence and inconsistent adverse-event reporting; current evidence did not support routine caffeine use in youth sport.

Thirteen-study hemodialysis review found selected CRP reductions with omega-3 formulations but substantial heterogeneity and poor adverse-event reporting; reported events were mostly mild, while optimal formulation/composition remains uncertain.

Systematic review of recent Serenoa repens evidence found symptom improvements in some BPH/LUTS studies and generally favorable tolerability, but extract/formulation, combination-treatment and study-design heterogeneity substantially limited comparability.

Umbrella meta-analysis found dietary therapies such as low-glycemic-index treatment reduced seizure frequency while antioxidant adjuncts did not show significant efficacy; adverse events increased overall, especially with ketogenic diets, so this remains broad category evidence.

Six-RCT/438-participant septic-shock meta-analysis found lower in-hospital mortality and renal-replacement-therapy use with thiamin; critically ill population and treatment-context boundaries prevent extrapolation to general supplementation.

Meta-analysis of three adult RCTs found small reductions in stress and anxiety with bovine milk-fat-globule-membrane supplementation, while depression effects were nonsignificant; the evidence base is only three trials and remains preliminary.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found lower circulating short-chain fatty acids in depression and six RCTs suggested probiotic/prebiotic interventions can raise fecal SCFAs alongside symptom improvement; biomarker associations do not establish a specific supplement mechanism or strain effect.

Systematic review of 122 psychiatric nutraceutical studies found heterogeneous signals across vitamin D, NAC, acetyl-L-carnitine, CoQ10, alpha-lipoic acid, magnesium and B vitamins, with high overall risk of bias and low methodological quality; category-level evidence only.

Thirteen-RCT/710-participant meta-analysis in major depressive disorder found a small pooled symptom benefit favoring probiotics with moderate heterogeneity; strain/formulation uncertainty prevents generic probiotic equivalence.

Scoping review found very limited human mood evidence for gotu kola, phosphatidylcholine and taurine, with most supporting data preclinical and no studies of their combination; evidence is insufficient for quantitative synthesis or product-level claims.

Systematic review of 56 controlled human/animal studies found sleep-related signals from probiotics, prebiotics, dietary patterns and botanicals, but major intervention heterogeneity and mixed preclinical/human evidence prevent attribution to a single compound or strain.

Four-RCT schizophrenia meta-analysis found no significant effect on positive or total symptoms, a small low-certainty reduction in negative symptoms, and very uncertain effects on depression/general psychopathology; authors did not recommend clinical implementation.

Meta-analysis of 16 RCTs across curcumin, ascorbic acid, resveratrol and sulforaphane found non-robust and compound-specific schizophrenia signals; formulation/co-intervention heterogeneity and sparse data for several agents require category-level handling.

Network meta-analysis of 25 RCTs in PCOS found potential mood benefits for omega-3 plus vitamin E among several psychological/exercise/drug interventions, while vitamin D plus probiotics was not significantly beneficial; combined-intervention attribution firewall applies.

Four RCTs/1,342 women without diagnosed mental illness found limited strain-specific probiotic signals for perinatal depressive/anxiety symptoms; no prebiotic or synbiotic trials were available and risk of bias was moderate-to-high.

Systematic review of four probiotic studies in fibromyalgia found inconsistent anxiety/depression effects and insufficient safety reporting, so no definitive recommendation for or against probiotics could be made.

Systematic review of non-pharmacological/non-psychological depression augmentation found lower levels of evidence for probiotics than for exercise or bright-light approaches; augmentation evidence remains category-specific and does not establish probiotic monotherapy efficacy.

Systematic review of six prospective cohorts and four RCTs in IBD linked dysbiosis with anxiety/depression and found microbiota-targeted interventions sometimes improved symptoms, but interventions included probiotics and fecal microbiota transplantation and remained heterogeneous.

Meta-analysis of seven intervention RCTs found pooled depressive-symptom improvement from diverse SCFA-modulating strategies, including probiotics, FMT, vagal stimulation and direct butyrate; between-class differences were not significant and the evidence cannot be assigned to one supplement.

Nine-study/617-participant meta-analysis in MCI/Alzheimer/dementia found modest cognitive-score improvements with ginseng, but effects did not reach clear clinical significance and evidence was limited by small study count and heterogeneity.

Dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies associated higher dietary choline intake with lower risk of cognitive decline and Alzheimer-related outcomes, but this is non-randomized dietary evidence and cannot establish supplementation efficacy or an optimal supplemental dose.

Translational Parkinson review found consistent preclinical neuroprotection and small open-label human signals in UPDRS/DAT imaging, but randomized efficacy evidence was lacking; disease-modifying claims remain premature.

Seven placebo-controlled RCTs/566 participants found no consistent NAC benefit for alcohol craving or PTSD severity; a sensitivity-analysis signal emerged only after one study was removed, supporting an overall null/uncertain efficacy interpretation.

Meta-analysis of 74 RCTs found apparent adjunctive benefits for several anti-inflammatory agents including NAC and fatty acids, but publication bias, heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses weakened many effects; routine use was not robustly supported.

VaD-focused RCT meta-analysis found small cognitive effects for galantamine/memantine and a fragile very-low-certainty EGb 761 signal, while citicoline and several other interventions remained single-trial/non-poolable; patient-important benefits were uncertain.

Systematic review of eight acute RCTs/244 healthy participants found mostly null or small inconsistent taurine cognition/mood effects; more reliable benefits occurred in caffeine combinations that did not isolate taurine.

Small four-arm RCT in 36 peri/postmenopausal women found medium-dose creatine hydrochloride improved selected reaction-time, brain-creatine and lipid outcomes versus placebo, but sample size, formulation specificity and exploratory endpoints sharply limit generalization to creatine monohydrate.

Parallel trial in 40 young active adults found creatine monohydrate improved Wingate mean/peak power but did not improve Stroop or Trail cognitive outcomes; useful direct null evidence against broad acute cognition claims in healthy active adults.

Sleep-deprivation crossover trial in 29 healthy adults found a single creatine dose attenuated deterioration in several cognitive tasks during 21 hours of sleep loss; acute sleep-deprivation context and unusually large studied exposure prevent routine cognition/dosing extrapolation.

Meta-analysis of 16 pediatric ADHD RCTs found a small borderline overall PUFA benefit with stronger signals on performance-based cognition than subjective ratings; heterogeneity was substantial and PUFA supplementation was not supported as standalone treatment.

Seven-RCT meta-analysis in postmenopausal women found small gains in lean mass and leg-press strength, especially when creatine was paired with resistance training, while bone density was unchanged; effects were context-dependent and safety signals were mild.

Systematic review of eight small clinical studies found creatine alone had limited clinical benefit in chronic musculoskeletal pain, while creatine plus resistance exercise sometimes improved strength, muscle mass and selected quality-of-life outcomes; pain/inflammation results were inconsistent.

Stratified systematic review found vitamin D benefits were most consistent in deficient older/clinical populations, while elite-athlete performance, BMD and fracture outcomes in broadly replete adults were often null; supports deficiency correction rather than universal ergogenic use.

Systematic review of 101 studies found acute sodium-bicarbonate protocols commonly produced gastrointestinal symptoms that increased with single-dose exposure; spread dosing and alternative delivery formats may reduce symptoms, but direct comparative evidence remains insufficient.

Systematic review of 26 controlled studies found exogenous ketones reliably raised beta-hydroxybutyrate and altered metabolism, but exercise-performance effects ranged from benefit to null or impairment and depended heavily on protocol/co-ingestion context.

Bayesian network meta-analysis of 13 co-supplementation trials found small performance benefits from caffeine, sodium bicarbonate and their combination versus placebo, but no clear evidence that co-ingestion outperformed either supplement alone despite larger metabolic changes.

Meta-analysis of 12 resistance-training studies in young adults found no significant lean-mass advantage from whey or soy supplementation, while whey improved bench-press and squat strength; protein type, training context and small study count limit generalization.

Network meta-analysis of 18 RCTs/1,341 older adults found protein-related supplementation added to exercise improved grip strength and ASMI but not TUG overall; HMB/whey/leucine rankings were exploratory because certainty was very low and the network sparse.

Small eight-week RCT in 18 healthy men found omega-3 supplementation altered oxylipins and attenuated peak strength loss after eccentric muscle damage, but soreness did not differ; mechanistic recovery signal from a very small sample.

Meta-analysis of 41 RCTs found moderate reductions in selected post-exercise inflammatory/muscle-damage markers and soreness with EPA/DHA, but subgroup patterns reflected heterogeneous doses, durations and athlete populations; biomarker recovery is not equivalent to performance enhancement.

Network meta-analysis of 35 trials suggested outcome-specific rankings: creatine for strength, protein for endurance and omega-3 for recovery; indirect ranking evidence should not be treated as head-to-head proof of superiority.

Secondary randomized analysis in older adults undergoing exercise found omega-3 selectively lowered PGE2 while several other lipid/inflammatory mediators changed similarly in both groups; biomarker modulation did not establish a functional performance benefit.

Eight-week active-comparator RCT in 28 young men found structured EPA/MCT lipid increased serum EPA:AA more than a physical mixture but did not improve muscular endurance or fatigue outcomes; direct biomarker-versus-performance dissociation.

Systematic review of 53 RCTs across vitamin D, leucine, omega-3 and probiotics found generally favorable but heterogeneous muscle-function signals with mostly low/very-low certainty; multi-agent category evidence cannot be converted into a universal sarcopenia recommendation.

Triple-crossover RCT in recreationally trained adults found six weeks of high-intensity functional training improved performance, but added fish protein+vitamin D+omega-3 did not enhance measured adaptations versus whey or maltodextrin controls.

Twelve-week placebo-controlled trial in trained adults found microencapsulated DHA increased omega-3 index and reduced post-eccentric-exercise soreness with selected neuromuscular/inflammatory differences; formulation and exercise-recovery context remain explicit.

Systematic review of 11 human studies found inconsistent neuromuscular effects from long-chain omega-3 supplementation, with numerous null and some context-specific adverse findings; current evidence remains limited and heterogeneous.

Systematic review of 15 sport/exercise RCTs found selected oxidative-stress and recovery signals but inconsistent muscle-damage, inflammation, soreness/fatigue and performance effects; certainty ranged from low to very low.

Small randomized crossover pilot in 12 resistance-trained adults found 12 g but not 8 g citrulline malate modestly increased leg-press repetitions, with no broad dose-response conclusion justified from the tiny sample.

Randomized crossover trial in 16 highly trained male taekwondo athletes found combined citrulline malate plus L-arginine improved selected anaerobic, agility and jump outcomes versus placebo/single-supplement conditions; combination design prevents single-ingredient attribution.

Randomized crossover trial in collegiate wrestlers found acute beetroot juice plus vitamin C improved selected Wingate power outcomes and lowered post-exercise glucose, while CK and LDH were unchanged; co-supplementation prevents beetroot-only attribution.

Randomized double-blind trial in 12 elite swimmers found acute beetroot juice did not improve repeated 200-m performance, lactate or perceived exertion under competition-like conditions; useful elite-performance null evidence.

Very small crossover pilot in 10 amateur triathletes found beetroot nitrate strongly increased NO-pathway and several oxidative/inflammatory biomarkers without clear lipid-oxidative damage; functional performance significance was not established.

Randomized crossover trial in 15 trained male cyclists found nitrate, caffeine and their combination did not significantly change end power, work above end power, peak power, mean power or total work during a 3-min all-out test.

Randomized double-blind trial in 12 trained male sprinters found beetroot juice markedly raised salivary nitrate/nitrite but did not improve jump height, 60/100-m sprint performance or most neuromuscular measures; direct biomarker-performance null.

Network meta-analysis of 16 PCOS RCTs found GLP-1 receptor agonist plus metformin most effective for weight/BMI, while inositol-containing strategies were less prominent and none of the compared interventions significantly improved HOMA-IR; comparative pharmacologic context, not an inositol efficacy endorsement.

Meta-analysis of 13 RCTs/1,325 postmenopausal women found soy isoflavones improved vaginal dryness and urogenital symptoms, while vasomotor and psychological outcomes were nonsignificant and heterogeneity exceeded 90%; formulation/population boundaries remain explicit.

Systematic review of 11 PCOS studies found deficiency common and supplementation effects on insulin sensitivity and reproductive outcomes modest/inconsistent; correction of deficiency may complement care but vitamin D was not supported as stand-alone PCOS or fertility therapy.

Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs/992 reproductive-age women found no overall effect of vitamin D supplementation on anti-Müllerian hormone, with substantial heterogeneity; open-label subgroup findings did not override the double-blind null.

Systematic review found lower maternal selenium concentrations associated with miscarriage in observational studies, but randomized interventional evidence was absent and confounding substantial; no causal supplementation claim is authorized.

Systematic review of selenium exposure and congenital anomalies found mixed observational associations by anomaly type, with only one randomized trial identified; evidence is confounded and insufficient to define an optimal supplemental selenium level in pregnancy.

Meta-analysis of three studies/288 Hashimoto patients with subclinical hypothyroidism found myo-inositol plus selenium lowered TSH more than selenium alone, while T3/T4/TPOAb were not significantly different and the tiny evidence base limits confidence.

Meta-analysis/trial-sequential analysis of 16 phytoestrogen RCTs found improvement in selected menopausal psychological symptoms, but effects varied by symptom and menopausal stage and some significant outcomes failed sequential correction; category-level evidence only.

Systematic review of 15 RCTs found soy-based dietary patterns may reduce hot-flash frequency/severity, while overall vasomotor and psychological effects were inconsistent and certainty very low; whole-food/dietary evidence is not equivalent to supplement-only efficacy.

Meta-analysis of 23 pregnancy studies found modest increases in gestational weight gain and infant birth size plus lower preterm-birth risk with omega-3 supplementation, but sensitivity analyses weakened some outcomes and effects remained outcome-specific.

Meta-analysis of 21 prenatal DHA RCTs found no significant benefit across measured offspring neurodevelopmental domains, with only a modest birth-weight increase among growth outcomes; direct counterweight to broad prenatal cognition claims.

Systematic review found only two pregnancy studies linking omega-3 interventions/exposure with LC-MS oxylipin profiling, leaving mechanistic relationships with gestational length and preterm birth insufficient and hypothesis-generating.

Male-infertility meta-analysis found no significant improvement in human semen parameters with astaxanthin despite strong animal-model effects; human fertility outcomes such as pregnancy were not assessed, so clinical efficacy is unsupported.

Meta-analysis of five studies after varicocelectomy found no consistent additional benefit of vitamin E on sperm concentration or motility, with heterogeneous morphology/pregnancy reporting; useful null evidence against routine postoperative vitamin-E claims.

Meta-analysis of 41 RCTs in idiopathic male infertility found antioxidant-associated improvements in semen parameters, but prediction intervals crossed the null, heterogeneity exceeded 80%, certainty was very low, and live-birth evidence was inadequate.

Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs/618 women with PCOS pooled magnesium, chromium, zinc, selenium and chromium-picolinate interventions and found improved glycemic/selected lipid measures, but the mixed-mineral design prevents attributing effects to any single mineral.

Nine-RCT meta-analysis in older adults found small pooled immune-function improvements across diverse micronutrients, with vitamin D, vitamin E and multivitamin subgroup signals; heterogeneous multi-nutrient evidence should not be reduced to a single supplement claim.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found no high-certainty evidence that dietary supplements improve female infertility outcomes versus placebo; secondary signals for NAC, myo-inositol, vitamin D/E and combinations were hypothesis-generating and at higher risk of bias.

Meta-analysis in iodine-deficient pregnant women found iodine supplementation lowered TSH and thyroglobulin, with subgroup differences by region, trimester, regimen and iodine form; biochemical improvement does not establish universal dosing outside deficiency context.

Systematic review of 22 studies linked maternal B12, vitamin D and folate status with child neurodevelopment, but 18 of 22 studies were observational and heterogeneity precluded quantitative synthesis; strongest causal inference remains limited.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 24 preconception studies found selected maternal/neonatal benefits from lifestyle and nutritional interventions, but mixed study designs, heterogeneous interventions and outcome-specific pooling constrain causal supplement claims.

Network meta-analysis of 11 GDM RCTs ranked different supplements favorably for different birth outcomes, but no single intervention improved all maternal/newborn outcomes and several rankings were based on wide credible intervals; network rankings remain exploratory.

ART meta-analysis found resveratrol improved fertilization rate but did not significantly improve biochemical/clinical pregnancy, live birth, oocyte count or embryo outcomes overall; fertility-establishment and live-birth nulls remain first-class.

Systematic review reported favorable ART-related signals with melatonin in PCOS, including endometrial thickness, oocyte/embryo quality and pregnancy measures, but heterogeneous observational/clinical evidence and regimen variation limit confidence; no consumer dosing inference.

Meta-analysis of oral antioxidant RCTs in IVF/ICSI reported improved pregnancy and selected laboratory outcomes plus a live-birth signal, but regimens were heterogeneous, study count limited and certainty insufficient for a single antioxidant or standardized protocol recommendation.

Open-label randomized comparison in emotionally dysregulated youth found omega-3 plus inositol and N-acetylcysteine each produced modest mania/depression improvements without a clear overall between-group winner; autism-trait status appeared to modify some NAC responses, so the combination cannot be attributed to omega-3 alone.

Small double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 40 patients receiving adjuvant breast-cancer chemotherapy found melatonin improved selected sleep-quality measures across treatment, while anxiety/depression signals were phase-dependent and the disease-specific sample limits generalization.

Twelve-week randomized creatine trial in middle-aged and older adults reported gains in lean mass, strength and selected cognitive/memory measures with and without exercise/diet intervention; cognitive and biomarker findings were explicitly exploratory and the exercise-versus-nonexercise allocation was not randomized.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 70 head-and-neck cancer patients with sleep disturbance found 14 days of oral melatonin improved PSQI sleep scores and fatigue versus placebo; evidence is short-term and disease-context specific.

Six-week exploratory trial in 58 healthy adults found guanidinoacetic acid, alone or with creatine, produced selected reaction-time and stress signals while many cognitive domains were unchanged and some sleep effects were potentially undesirable; multi-arm design prevents simple creatine attribution.

Systematic evidence map of matcha and green-tea bioactives found lower caffeine-plus-EGCG to theanine-plus-arginine preparations were more consistently associated with cortisol-related stress signals, but evidence mixed human, animal and in-vitro studies and GRADE certainty was low to very low.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 65 gastrointestinal-cancer survivors found four weeks of standardized Panax ginseng reduced cancer-related fatigue and improved several daily-function domains, with no treatment-related adverse events reported; findings remain short-term and population-specific.

Small exploratory MRS study in older adults assigned to Bacopa formulations or ghee reported preliminary neurometabolite and cognitive changes after three months; intervention groups were tiny and the study was not a definitive efficacy trial.

Pre-planned item-level analysis from a 498-participant randomized trial found the proprietary lavender-oil preparation Silexan improved several MADRS symptom items versus placebo with a profile broadly similar to sertraline; this is formulation-specific and secondary/exploratory evidence.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 56 adults with low mood found a standardized saffron formulation improved mood, affect, DASS-21, sleep quality and cortisol over 56 days; small sample size and proprietary formulation require cautious generalization.

Single-blind randomized trial in pulmonary sarcoidosis found 60 days of saffron plus sleep-hygiene counseling improved PSQI, daytime sleepiness, fatigue and quality-of-life measures versus counseling alone; disease context and lack of double blinding limit generalization.

Large multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial after COVISHIELD vaccination found 24 weeks of standardized ashwagandha had safety and tolerability comparable to placebo, while exploratory immunogenicity and breakthrough-infection outcomes showed no clear intervention benefit.

Systematic review of 14 older-adult studies found probiotic, prebiotic and synbiotic interventions sometimes improved cognition, with a small pooled global-cognition signal in a subgroup; intervention heterogeneity and limited high-quality evidence prevent class-wide efficacy claims.

Open-label 12-week pilot in 30 adults with depressive and anxiety symptoms reported large within-person improvements during multi-strain probiotic use, but the absence of a placebo or control group prevents causal attribution.

Three-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled menopause trial found a multi-ingredient supplement containing L-theanine, GABA, magnesium, SAM-e and propyl gallate improved sleep disturbance, sleep-related impairment, total sleep time and sleep efficiency; ingredient-specific attribution is not possible.

Randomized placebo-controlled trial in intensive-care nurses found bedtime aromatherapy massage with chamomile-lavender or vetiver improved fatigue and PSQI sleep scores more than jojoba placebo over four weeks; results apply to an olfactory/topical intervention rather than oral supplementation.

Open-label randomized hemodialysis trial found a combined lavender/bergamot essential-oil plus herbal-sachet intervention improved self-reported sleep and anxiety versus usual care over three months; combined exposure and inability to blind prevent single-ingredient attribution.

Systematic review of nine schizophrenia RCTs found selected metabolic, inflammatory and neuropsychiatric signals across probiotics, vitamin combinations, omega-3 and plant-derived bioactives, but substantial intervention heterogeneity and short follow-up preclude a unified nutritional recommendation.

Systematic review of 22 clinical and preclinical studies found omega-3, ketogenic, B-vitamin, vitamin D and microbiota-targeted interventions can modulate neuroinflammatory biomarkers, but evidence strength varied widely and much of the ketogenic/mechanistic support was preclinical.

Small randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 24 under-19 soccer players found CoQ10 and taurine produced different oxidative, inflammatory and hormonal biomarker patterns during repeated match simulations; tiny groups and biomarker focus do not establish broad performance superiority.

Randomized trial in 60 children with inappropriate sinus tachycardia found three months of omega-3 improved heart-rate and heart-rate-variability measures versus standard follow-up, while anxiety scores did not differ; findings are condition-specific and require replication.

Double-blind three-way crossover trial in 21 adolescents with ADHD found an acute L-theanine-plus-caffeine combination reduced false alarms and altered P3b measures versus placebo, while hits and discrimination sensitivity were unchanged and only methylphenidate improved overall reaction time; combination attribution remains explicit.

Secondary analysis in a predefined 12-person subpopulation receiving a phospholipid-based Melissa officinalis formulation found salivary cortisol fell over three weeks alongside improved sleep and mood measures; tiny uncontrolled secondary analysis is hypothesis-generating only.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 66 postmenopausal women found 12 weeks of ashwagandha root extract improved PSQI sleep quality, menopausal symptoms, body-fat percentage and several quality-of-life domains, while bone mineral density did not differ; single-center population limits generalization.

Small randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 24 competitive male football players reported improved intermittent performance, selected sprint and decision-making outcomes and lower post-exercise lactate after four weeks of Rhodiola rosea; numerous endpoints and tiny groups make the findings exploratory.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial in 35 healthy adults found six weeks of dried ginger increased ex-vivo cholesterol efflux capacity and improved oxidative-stress response, while conventional lipids, body weight and blood pressure were unchanged; mechanistic cardiovascular signals should not be equated with clinical event reduction.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of seven TMD RCTs found oral glucosamine did not provide a clinically important pain reduction in temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis or other TMD, although selected quality-of-life or functional outcomes may improve; adverse-event certainty was very low.

Umbrella review of 19 reviews found glucosamine produced small VAS pain and joint-space-narrowing signals but no significant WOMAC pain or functional improvement; most source reviews were low or critically low quality and clinical importance remained uncertain.

Network meta-analysis of 60 RCTs in adults with overweight or obesity found outcome-specific inflammatory biomarker signals across green tea extract, curcumin, synbiotics, zinc and probiotic-plus-omega-3 combinations; indirect rankings and mixed interventions do not support a single universal supplement recommendation.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 60 adults with mild-to-moderate knee osteoarthritis found a standardized water-dispersible Boswellia extract improved WOMAC, pain, stiffness and hs-CRP over eight weeks; results are proprietary-formulation specific and need independent replication.

Meta-analysis of randomized trials in type 2 diabetes found curcumin/curcuminoids lowered hs-CRP and TNF-alpha on average, but the evidence base was small, TNF-alpha heterogeneity was substantial and several reporting/unit issues increased uncertainty.

Secondary molecular analysis from a prior 30-person placebo-controlled knee-osteoarthritis trial found nano-micelle curcumin reduced T-bet expression and correlated with CD8-positive T-cell changes, while GATA3 was unchanged; mechanistic secondary data do not establish independent clinical efficacy.

Partially randomized patient-preference trial in vitamin-D-insufficient young people with major depression found no overall randomized-group improvement in depression versus placebo, although anxiety improved and moderate-to-severe subgroups showed exploratory signals; preference and subgroup analyses require caution.

Double-blind placebo-controlled 24-week trial in 87 older adults with early cognitive impairment found multistrain probiotics lowered plasma pTau181 and selectively preserved visuospatial/certain clinical cognition measures, while MMSE, verbal memory and executive outcomes showed no significant between-group differences.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 48 healthy adults found Bacillus coagulans BCP92 caused no major microbiome-composition shift, with only subtle taxa and short-chain-fatty-acid changes; useful evidence against overstating microbiome remodeling in healthy users.

Single-center open-label randomized study after colonoscopy found probiotic supplementation was associated with faster microbiota-diversity recovery, particularly in ulcerative colitis, but outcomes were primarily microbiome/predicted-pathway measures and open-label design limits clinical inference.

Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled six-month trial in 72 adults with stage 3-4 chronic kidney disease reported improved eGFR trajectory with Lactobacillus plantarum versus placebo, while urinary indoxyl sulfate did not differ; single modest-size trial requires replication before disease-modifying claims.

Four-week placebo-controlled study in 32 combat-sport athletes during weight reduction found probiotic supplementation was associated with larger body-fat and selected lipid/fatty-acid changes; concurrent weight cutting and small sample size make probiotic-specific performance or weight-loss claims inappropriate.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 RCTs/920 participants with COPD found modest pooled pulmonary-function and inflammatory-marker improvements with probiotics, but strain/regimen heterogeneity and disease-specific populations limit class-wide generalization.

Multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 44 children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis found VSL#3 did not improve the primary disease-activity response and increased fecal TLR4 agonist activity, while microbiota diversity, permeability and systemic cytokines were unchanged; important null/safety-mechanism counterweight.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 12-week trial in 102 women with obesity found a three-strain probiotic altered selected endocrine/appetite markers, body-composition measures, mood scores and gut taxa; multi-strain formulation and multiple endpoints require formulation-specific interpretation.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 48 healthy men found four weeks of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum GKK1 attenuated selected post-exercise performance decrements and muscle-damage/inflammatory markers after a muscle-damage protocol; strain-specific and short-term exercise context remain explicit.

Systematic review of 29 adult RCTs found lifestyle and psychobiotic interventions sometimes improved stress-related outcomes alongside microbiome changes, but no consistent taxonomic or diversity signature explained favorable responses; mechanistic microbiome narratives remain heterogeneous.

Twelve-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in overweight adults found Weissella confusa WIKIM51 improved triglycerides and selected abdominal-fat measures, supported by preclinical GLP-1 findings; strain-specific clinical outcomes should not be generalized to probiotics as a class.

Meta-analysis of 18 osteoarthritis RCTs found gut-microbiota-targeted interventions reduced several pain/function and inflammatory outcomes, while stiffness, body weight, knee flexion, COMP and IL-6 were null; all trials had at least some risk-of-bias concerns and interventions were heterogeneous.

Meta-analysis of nine placebo-controlled studies/649 adults with type 2 diabetes reported pooled reductions in fasting glucose, HbA1c and insulin with probiotics; strain differences, selection criteria and adjunct-to-standard-care context prevent a generic treatment claim.

Secondary analysis of a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled PCOS trial found 12 weeks of a nine-strain probiotic produced no significant between-group improvement in glucose homeostasis, HOMA-IR or lipid profile; useful metabolic null evidence despite limited precision and attrition.

Open-label randomized trial in 60 breast-cancer patients receiving weekly paclitaxel found adjunctive CoQ10 was associated with less grade-2-or-higher neuropathy, delayed neuropathy onset and selected fatigue, insomnia, hematologic and cardiac-function signals; open-label supportive-care context requires confirmation.

Network meta-analysis of 23 knee-osteoarthritis RCTs compared celecoxib, probiotics, metformin, krill oil and glucosamine/chondroitin; auxiliary-intervention rankings were mostly low or very-low certainty and indirect, so SUCRA ordering should not be treated as head-to-head superiority.

Meta-analysis of 32 RCTs/4,010 patients found Lactobacillus added to H. pylori eradication therapy modestly increased eradication success and reduced adverse events overall, with benefits varying by antibiotic regimen and age; evidence concerns adjunctive treatment, not probiotic monotherapy.

Meta-analysis of 25 RCTs/25,578 patients with established cardiovascular disease found combined EPA+DHA did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiovascular events or atrial fibrillation/postoperative atrial fibrillation; formulation, dose and background therapy may explain heterogeneity, but pooled clinical benefit was neutral.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials in psychotic disorders found omega-3 supplementation did not consistently improve BMI, waist circumference, glucose, lipids or blood pressure; isolated subgroup signals did not survive pooled analysis.

Nine-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled pilot in adults with coeliac disease and hypercholesterolemia found a combined Lactiplantibacillus-plus-plant-sterol/stanol formulation improved selected lipid and microbiome measures; small pilot design and combination exposure prevent ingredient-specific attribution.

Meta-analysis of 12 older RCTs/779 patients with CKD-associated anemia reported higher hemoglobin and lower erythropoietin requirements with vitamin D supplementation, but the evidence corpus ended in 2018 and authors called for larger modern multicenter trials.

Network meta-analysis comparing nutraceutical interventions for flow-mediated dilation in cardiovascular disease/hypertension ranked magnesium and vitamin D3 highly, with signals for flaxseed, barberry, folic acid and omega-3; indirect network rankings and variable certainty are not head-to-head proof.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 12-week trial in adults with mild hypertriglyceridemia found a two-strain probiotic combination reduced triglycerides and LDL from baseline and altered selected glucose/microbiome measures; per-protocol analysis and formulation specificity limit generalization.

Meta-analysis of randomized trials in hemodialysis patients found omega-3 supplementation did not reduce all-cause mortality but was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality, myocardial infarction and vascular-access events; much of the event signal was concentrated in one large trial.

Open-label randomized 24-week trial in 38 heart-failure patients compared Mediterranean diet alone with diet plus omega-3-enriched oral nutritional supplements and found complex lipidomic changes that varied by sarcopenia status; combination exposure and small sample preclude omega-3-only attribution.

Multimodal study combining Mendelian randomization, proteomic mediation and meta-analysis of 12 RCTs linked higher omega-3 status with lower DKD risk and reported selected supplementation benefits, but causal-genetic, mechanistic and trial evidence should remain analytically distinct.

Systematic review/meta-analysis in CKD found higher observational vitamin-D status correlated with lower left-ventricular mass, but supplementation did not significantly improve LV mass index or ejection fraction; a possible septal-thickness signal was based on limited inconsistent evidence.

Dose-response meta-analysis of 78 RCTs found small average improvements in several cardiometabolic markers with magnesium, including blood pressure, glucose, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, LDL, triglycerides and IL-6, while many anthropometric, liver, kidney and inflammatory outcomes were null.

Meta-analysis and trial-sequential analysis of nine RCTs/644 participants with diabetic nephropathy found probiotics improved several creatinine, metabolic and inflammatory outcomes, but did not significantly improve eGFR or 24-hour proteinuria; renal-function claims should preserve these mixed endpoints.

Meta-analysis of 30 RCT publications/1,516 patients with MASLD found adjunctive probiotics/synbiotics improved ALT, AST, TNF-alpha and selected glucose/lipid markers, while triglycerides and overall HOMA-IR were null; subgroup effects varied by age, region, duration and diabetes status.

Cluster-randomized school trial in 306 adolescent girls in Ethiopia found weekly iron-folic acid supplementation reduced reported morbidity symptoms at later follow-up points, while growth-related effects were not broadly established; population and deficiency context remain essential.

Updated systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized trials compared intravenous with oral iron for pregnancy iron-deficiency anemia across maternal hematologic, transfusion, reaction and neonatal outcomes; evidence concerns treatment route in diagnosed anemia, not routine supplementation of iron-replete pregnancies.

Systematic mechanistic review across the lifespan found iron deficiency commonly associated with altered EEG/ERP patterns and delayed neural processing, with treatment-responsiveness evidence heterogeneous; electrophysiologic associations do not by themselves establish cognitive benefit from supplementation in iron-replete people.

Meta-analysis of 38 observational studies found lower serum vitamin D levels in thyroid disease, particularly autoimmune thyroid disorders, but the evidence is associative and cannot establish that vitamin D supplementation prevents or treats thyroid disease.

Network meta-analysis of eight randomized trials/4,078 high-risk pregnancies found some higher-dose vitamin-D regimens associated with lower estimated preeclampsia risk, but dose/regimen networks were sparse and indirect; no consumer dosing inference is authorized.

Post-hoc secondary analysis of a randomized pregnancy vitamin-D trial assessed offspring neuropsychological performance at age 10; because cognition was a later secondary endpoint and participants were unblinded years earlier, findings require cautious interpretation rather than broad prenatal-cognition claims.

Systematic review found replacing folic acid with 5-MTHF reduced circulating unmetabolized folic acid in a small trial set, while erythrocyte-folate results were discordant and observational UMFA-outcome associations were inconsistent and confounded; clinical harm from UMFA remains unresolved.

Randomized trial in 796 children with food allergy found a combined compound-probiotic, zinc and vitamin-B product plus hydrolyzed formula improved several allergy and immune markers versus formula alone; multi-component design prevents attribution to probiotics, zinc or B vitamins individually.

Preschool follow-up of a very small prenatal pilot RCT in folate-receptor-alpha-autoantibody-positive pregnancies reported fewer ASD diagnoses after folinic acid versus folic acid, but only 16 families were reassessed and confidence intervals were extremely wide; provocative pilot evidence only.

Pilot biomarker analysis from a randomized choline trial in 24 children with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder found no robust treatment-specific biomarker pattern after multiple-testing correction; brain-derived extracellular-vesicle changes were largely time effects rather than differential choline effects.

Reanalysis-style review of low-risk double-blind RCTs in adults aged 75+ found a small mortality signal favoring vitamin D, but no individual trial was confirmatory and the authors characterized the result as an evidence signal requiring confirmation.

Systematic/bibliometric review found biologically coherent links between selenium status and cardiovascular pathways, but supplementation trials were generally neutral or inconclusive and the translational evidence remained fragmented; status associations must not be converted into routine supplementation claims.

Small 24-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 41 older adults found a dehydroeffusol-enriched Juncus effusus extract improved selected Five-Cog clue-recall, clock-drawing and dexterity tasks; the sample was small and effects were outcome-specific.

Randomized double-blind crossover trial in adults with sleep complaints found a multi-ingredient evening blend containing mulberry leaf, tryptophan, zinc, magnesium and B vitamins shortened sleep-onset latency by about four minutes and improved selected next-morning mood measures; ingredient-specific attribution is not possible.

Network meta-analysis in older adults with mild cognitive impairment favored combined folate plus vitamin B12 for cognition and one-carbon-metabolism markers, but ranking evidence is indirect and should not be treated as proof of superiority across all MCI populations.

Meta-analysis of five randomized trials in young females with premenstrual syndrome found zinc supplementation improved pooled physical symptoms and several psychological and sleep-related subdomains; the small study base and multiple symptom outcomes limit precision.

Six-month double-blind randomized trial in 220 patients with cerebral-small-vessel-disease-related cognitive impairment found folic acid improved MoCA and MMSE scores while lowering homocysteine and MMP-9; findings are disease-specific and do not establish broad cognitive enhancement in healthy users.

The ZINCAiD randomized double-blind phase-II trial found no significant cognitive benefit for zinc versus placebo in the primary analysis; apparent stabilization emerged only in a post-hoc subgroup defined by ceruloplasmin response, making the responder finding exploratory.

Triple-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 50 adults with major depressive disorder found nano-selenium added to sertraline improved depressive symptoms and selected antioxidant markers over 12 weeks; the small sample, adjunctive design and nano-formulation prevent generalization to selenium monotherapy.

Microbiome analysis from a randomized placebo-controlled Synbiotic 2000 ADHD trial found no effect on taxonomic or functional alpha diversity, although beta-diversity and selected short-chain-fatty-acid patterns shifted; mechanistic microbiome changes should not be equated with clinical symptom efficacy.

Secondary analysis of the MADDY multinutrient ADHD trial linked zinc, selenium, copper, chromium and manganese changes to oxidative-stress markers, including possible pro-oxidant signals at higher selenium/chromium exposure; this is mechanistic multinutrient evidence, not single-mineral efficacy.

Three-arm trial in 84 IBS patients found zinc with or without probiotics improved serum zinc and GI symptom severity versus placebo, while zinc alone showed stronger depression and stress improvements than zinc-plus-probiotic; co-supplementation did not clearly add mood benefit.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of tomato and tomato-derived interventions found a small reduction in waist circumference but no consistent body-weight or BMI effect; benefits appeared more compatible with food-matrix cardiometabolic effects than with isolated lycopene-driven weight loss.

Eight-week double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 80 heart-failure patients found astaxanthin reduced TNF-alpha, MCP-1 and VLDL, while hs-CRP, most lipid measures and anthropometric outcomes were unchanged; selected biomarker effects do not establish clinical heart-failure benefit.

Very small randomized non-blinded pilot in 16 adults examined lutein/zeaxanthin exposure with versus without omega-3 co-supplementation over 12 days; the study primarily informs formulation and bioavailability questions and is too small for broad efficacy claims.

Randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial in postmenopausal women found a polyphenol mixture lowered oxidized-LDL measures but paradoxically increased total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and triglycerides in most completers; mixed biomarker direction is an important counterweight to simple antioxidant benefit claims.

Six-month randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 82 teenagers found lutein plus zeaxanthin increased macular pigment density and improved selected attention and processing-speed measures, while visual reasoning, nonverbal memory, gaming performance and self-reported sleep were unchanged.

Twenty-eight-day randomized double-masked placebo-controlled trial in young male taekwondo athletes found selected oxidative-stress and muscle-damage signals with astaxanthin, while most burnout dimensions showed no significant interaction; psychological-fatigue benefit was limited and exploratory.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase-II trial in 110 healthy lowland men ascending to high altitude found a quercetin food bar reduced acute-mountain-sickness incidence and severity and improved oxygen saturation and selected oxidative markers; evidence is specific to acclimatization at altitude.

Randomized triple-blind placebo-controlled trial in 52 adults with autism found within-group improvement in social-responsiveness scores with quercetin, but the between-group change was not statistically significant and quality-of-life signals weakened after adjustment; efficacy remains unconfirmed.

Double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial in 20 recreationally active women found two weeks of astaxanthin modestly lowered respiratory exchange ratio during submaximal cycling without changing heart rate, lactate or perceived exertion; substrate-use change is not evidence of improved exercise performance.

Systematic review and meta-analysis found lycopene-containing products modestly increased flow-mediated dilation in four studies totaling 182 healthy adults, but the signal lost statistical significance when one study was excluded; certainty was limited and the evidence base small.

Single-blind randomized pilot in 58 patients with active juvenile idiopathic arthritis found CoQ10 added to standard therapy improved JADAS-10, quality of life and inflammatory/oxidative markers over three months; modest size and adjunctive disease-specific design require replication.

Six-week double-blind randomized trial in 54 healthy active men found ubiquinol increased plasma CoQ10 and improved a mitochondrial coupling metric, but did not improve time-to-exhaustion or oxygen-uptake kinetics; direct mechanistic-versus-performance dissociation.

Randomized open-label crossover pharmacokinetic study found a proprietary liposomal CoQ10 formulation produced substantially higher AUC and Cmax than conventional CoQ10; this supports formulation-specific bioavailability, not superior clinical efficacy.

Double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 98 adults with MASLD found a proprietary carotenoid-rich tomato sauce reduced liver-fat CAP score more than commercial tomato-sauce control over 12 weeks; functional-food formulation and subgroup findings require independent replication.

Small double-blind randomized trial in 38 older adults completing eight weeks of HIIT found CoQ10 enhanced gains on two chair-stand lower-body tests, while grip strength, balance, mobility and walking endurance showed no between-group advantage; performance effects were narrow rather than global.

Meta-analysis of six randomized trials found MK-7 improved selected glycemic measures, but heterogeneity was very high and most other anthropometric/lipid outcomes were null; the small evidence base does not support broad metabolic efficacy claims.

Post-hoc analysis of a one-year randomized trial in women with low vitamin-K status found MK-7 lowered dp-ucMGP and attenuated vascular-stiffness progression in postmenopausal subgroups, especially those with higher baseline stiffness; subgroup/post-hoc design limits confirmatory inference.

AVADEC substudy in 388 older men found two years of vitamin K2 plus D3 markedly improved vitamin-K status but did not significantly change epicardial/pericoronary adipose inflammation or systemic inflammatory biomarkers; useful surrogate-target null evidence.

Meta-analysis of nine studies/2,570 postmenopausal osteoporosis patients found vitamin K2 improved several bone-turnover biomarkers, including osteocalcin carboxylation, while NTX was unchanged and clinical benefits such as fracture or BMD improvement remain unconfirmed.

Meta-analysis of eight RCTs in prediabetes/type-2 diabetes found modest reductions in fasting glucose, HbA1c and HOMA-IR with vitamin K, while fasting insulin and HOMA-beta were unchanged; isoform and duration heterogeneity limit treatment claims.

Twelve-week randomized double-blind trial in 71 young and older adults found vitamin K2 did not improve muscle strength, physical function, soreness or overall inflammatory recovery after muscle-damaging exercise; age-specific electrophysiologic and CK/IL-6 signals were exploratory.

Very small double-blind RCT in 20 older adults at cardiovascular risk found menaquinone-producing probiotics improved average dp-ucMGP and serum MK-7 over 12 weeks, but group differences diminished by week 12 and no clinical outcomes were tested.

Twelve-week randomized double-blind trial in 46 young adults with overweight/obesity found MK-4 lowered total and LDL cholesterol, while body composition, glucose metabolism and vitamin-K-dependent proteins were unchanged; small sample and multiple endpoints require replication.

Two-year randomized placebo-controlled trial in symptomatic coronary disease found MK-7 slowed progression of coronary calcium scores relative to placebo while strongly raising circulating MK-7; imaging progression is a surrogate and does not establish reduction in cardiovascular events.

Randomized double-blind crossover trial in 30 physically active older adults found creatine plus HMB during structured training improved several functional-strength/endurance measures, with little clear muscle-mass gain; combination exposure prevents attribution to either ingredient alone.

Double-blind crossover tracer study in 24 older adults found HMB added to a 40-g whey bolus further increased muscle-protein synthesis in older women and suppressed later protein breakdown; acute mechanistic responses do not establish long-term functional benefit.

Secondary post-hoc analysis of a critical-care HMB RCT found complex amino-acid and cytokine changes, including several higher pro-inflammatory cytokines in the HMB group; the findings challenge a simple anti-inflammatory narrative and remain exploratory.

Eight-week randomized trial of a prebiotic blend designed to promote Akkermansia increased its relative abundance and shifted selected taxa, with only a trend toward lower GI discomfort; microbiome changes were clearer than clinical effects.

Double-blind pilot RCT in 68 children with type-1 diabetes found oligofructose-enriched inulin enriched SCFA-producing taxa but did not significantly improve HbA1c over 12 weeks; microbiome modulation did not translate into short-term glycemic benefit.

Eight-week three-arm RCT in 99 young adults found both oatmeal and resistant-starch fiber diets lowered serum uric acid versus control, with a larger reduction in the oatmeal group; multi-omics mediation findings remain mechanistic and population-specific.

Eight-week double-blind placebo-controlled pediatric MASLD trial found a nine-strain synbiotic improved liver enzymes, lipids, BMI and ultrasound steatosis grade versus prebiotic-only placebo; short duration, combined formulation and surrogate liver measures require cautious interpretation.

Randomized double-blind psoriasis trial found chicory inulin-type fructans did not significantly improve body composition and largely stabilized metabolic variables while placebo worsened on some measures; authors cautioned that placebo composition may explain apparent differences.

Systematic review of 12 celiac-disease studies found prebiotic foods/supplements appeared generally safe and influenced SCFAs, microbiota and selected nutrient markers without compromising mucosal healing; intervention heterogeneity and mixed study designs prevent a class-wide efficacy claim.

Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs/780 women with PCOS found probiotics/synbiotics improved selected insulin, testosterone, lipid, BMI and antioxidant outcomes, while fasting glucose, HOMA-IR, several hormones and waist measures were null; effects were outcome-specific rather than global.

Small randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 50 women with obesity found an inulin-enriched tapioca product reduced body weight, body fat and selected lipid measures over 12 weeks; proprietary functional-food format and limited sample require replication.

Randomized controlled factorial trial in healthy adults found resistant starch and polydextrose produced distinct plasma/fecal bile-acid and microbiome associations; mechanistic bile-acid shifts should not be interpreted as proven clinical benefit.

Eight-week double-blind pilot in 30 women at metabolic-syndrome risk found resistant starch lowered systolic pressure within the intervention group, but the adjusted between-group difference was not significant and heart-rate-variability effects were exploratory.

Eight-week randomized placebo-controlled trial in 97 women with PCOS and metabolic syndrome found garlic improved several glucose, lipid, blood-pressure, inflammatory and quality-of-life measures; short follow-up and broad multiple-endpoint testing warrant replication.

Large double-blind placebo-controlled multicenter trial in 464 pregnant people with PCOS found myo-inositol did not reduce the composite risk of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia or preterm birth; strong direct null evidence against routine benefit in this population.

Umbrella meta-analysis reported lower gestational-diabetes and selected maternal/neonatal risks with inositol across prior meta-analyses, but the positive pooled signal should be reconciled with newer large direct RCT null findings such as PMID 40920401.

Randomized double-blind trial in 169 liver-transplant recipients found 30 days of taurine improved selected graft-function markers and was associated with shorter ICU/hospital stay, ventilation duration and lower mortality; single-center peri-transplant findings need independent replication.

Systematic review/meta-analysis pooled taurine trials from metabolic and inflammatory conditions plus convalescent taurine-status studies to argue biological relevance to long COVID; because the intervention trials were not direct PASC treatment trials, the evidence is indirect and should not be presented as established long-COVID efficacy.

Open-label randomized trial in 220 patients with decompensated cirrhosis found taurine did not significantly improve fatigue overall versus standard care; a large apparent benefit in the non-anemic subgroup was post hoc and hypothesis-generating.

Short randomized single-blind football trial found a taurine+caffeine+phosphatidylserine protocol improved selected physical, reaction-time and tactical outcomes versus placebo, but differing caffeine doses and multi-ingredient exposure prevent attribution to phosphatidylserine or taurine alone.

Double-blind placebo-controlled trial in men with idiopathic oligoasthenoteratozoospermia found CoQ10, L-carnitine and their combination improved semen measures and DNA fragmentation versus baseline/placebo, with the combination appearing stronger; fertility outcomes such as live birth were not established.

Randomized double-blind pilot in hemodialysis patients hyporesponsive to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents found intravenous L-carnitine reduced erythropoietin resistance index versus placebo; the small pilot and specialized treatment population limit generalization.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 15 studies/809 participants reported lower depressive symptoms with acetyl-L-carnitine versus placebo and broadly comparable effects to antidepressants, but the corpus mixed RCTs, open-label and observational designs and needs larger confirmatory trials.

Double-blind randomized crossover challenge study found a single pomegranate-extract dose did not reduce post-carnitine TMAO exposure overall in healthy high producers; age/sex subgroup signals were post hoc and require confirmation.

Meta-analysis of 16 trials/699 hemodialysis patients found no significant overall effect of L-carnitine on weight, BMI, triglycerides, LDL, total cholesterol, HDL, albumin or hemoglobin; favorable subgroup findings were exploratory and vulnerable to multiple-testing error.

Meta-analysis of ten RCTs in women with overweight/obesity found modest reductions in triglycerides, total cholesterol and LDL with L-carnitine, while HDL was unchanged; dose/duration subgroup findings remain exploratory.

Bayesian network meta-analysis of nine RCTs found route-dependent alpha-lipoic-acid effects in diabetic peripheral neuropathy, but apparent sequential-therapy superiority disappeared after excluding high-bias evidence; route rankings should not be treated as simple universal superiority.

Double-blind placebo-controlled crossover pilot in 20 IBS-D patients found oral GABA improved IBS symptom score and selected emotional/inflammatory measures without substantial microbiome remodeling; very small sample makes the result preliminary.

Randomized double-blind crossover study in bipolar disorder plus alcohol-use disorder found one-week NAC lowered dACC glutamate/glutamine and heavy-drinking days versus placebo, while depressive symptoms were unchanged; short mechanistic trial requires larger clinical confirmation.
