Tiny three-month randomized placebo-controlled pilot in 18 older adults found blueberry powder changed selected gut-microbial enzyme functions but not species abundance, metabolites or between-group depressive symptoms; microbiome signals were preliminary.

Bayesian network meta-analysis suggested caffeine+taurine may outperform either alone for selected anaerobic and reaction-time outcomes, while endurance and physiologic responses were variable; indirect network rankings and combination exposure prevent single-ingredient claims.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 109 T2D RCTs found outcome-specific antioxidant/glycemic signals across ALA, vitamin D, curcumin, NAC, citrulline, taurine, zinc, selenium and chromium; heterogeneous category-level evidence cannot justify a universal antioxidant-supplement recommendation.

Focused evidence synthesis concluded that diet quality, omega-3s, microbiota-targeted foods and micronutrients show modest, context-dependent mood signals, with the most defensible strategy being food-first and correction of insufficiency rather than blanket supplementation.

Open-label randomized trial in 60 non-diabetic MASLD patients found high-dose NAC added to lifestyle intervention did not improve oxidative stress, insulin resistance, FibroScan steatosis/fibrosis or most metabolic outcomes versus lifestyle alone; strong direct null evidence.

Randomized controlled day-surgery study in older adults found perioperative oral NAC did not improve early postoperative MoCA scores or discharge readiness, though quality-of-recovery scores were higher; cognitive-protection efficacy was not demonstrated.

One-year randomized placebo-controlled Parkinson pilot found more favorable exploratory UPDRS and dopamine-transporter imaging trajectories with NAC among completers, but only 32 completed follow-up, multiplicity was uncorrected and the study does not establish disease modification.

Double-blind randomized pilot in 51 women with preeclampsia found NAC did not materially alter redox/inflammatory markers or delivery mode; a gestational-age difference lost significance after covariate adjustment and remains exploratory.

Review of oral GABA as a functional nutrient found extensive mechanistic/preclinical rationale but limited human evidence and no definitive clinical efficacy; future work needs powered RCTs, dose-response and long-term safety data.

Very small double-blind crossover trial in 14 firefighters found caffeinated chewing gum improved a functional-balance test after GABA supplementation, with small-to-moderate effects; design cannot establish a GABA benefit and performance context is highly specific.

Meta-analysis of five RCTs/340 ICU respiratory patients found NAC did not significantly reduce mortality, mechanical-ventilation duration or ICU stay, although hospital stay was modestly shorter; core clinical outcomes were largely neutral.

Narrative review summarized mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence for acetyl-L-carnitine in peripheral neuropathies; useful background for neurotrophic/analgesic mechanisms but not a quantitative efficacy estimate.

Randomized trial in 44 older adults found concurrent training plus cricket protein hydrolysate improved selected blood-pressure-related measures versus placebo, but showed no clear added benefit over training or protein alone and did not uniquely improve arterial stiffness or most HRV outcomes.

Small randomized double-blind crossover trial in 24 adults with non-restorative sleep found a black-cumin-oil extract produced a distinct nocturnal melatonin profile and reduced daytime sleepiness/cortisol, while synthetic melatonin improved sleep latency and total sleep time more; active-comparator design and proprietary formulation limit generalization.

Single-blind randomized trial in 50 gastrointestinal-cancer surgery patients found BCAA-enriched supplementation after exercise did not significantly improve thigh muscle area, strength or six-minute-walk distance compared with amino-acid-free supplementation.

Systematic review and three-level meta-analysis found caffeine had no clear effect on perceptual or physiological recovery, a small possible benefit for functional performance, and worse sleep recovery; prediction intervals crossed the null and certainty varied by domain.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in adults with excess weight and GI discomfort found a heat-killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum postbiotic improved GSRS symptoms, perceived stress and digestion-related quality of life with microbiome shifts, while TNF-alpha, lipids and body composition were unchanged.

Randomized double-blind adjunctive trial in 60 H. pylori patients found IgY-enriched egg-yolk powder numerically improved eradication and symptom recovery, but the eradication difference was not statistically significant; promising adjunct signal without confirmatory efficacy.

Randomized double-blind trial in 87 adults with functional constipation found Pediococcus acidilactici PA53 improved stool form and altered gut microbiota, while between-group bowel-movement-frequency and biomarker differences were not significant.

Randomized double-blind trial in 24 trained male cyclists found 14 days of chickpea protein hydrolysate improved selected LDH and CRP responses after training, while body composition and direct recovery/performance outcomes were not improved or not measured.

Meta-analysis of randomized trials found corn-derived dietary fibers lowered total and LDL cholesterol modestly, while glycemic control, other lipids, anthropometrics, blood pressure and CRP were unchanged.

Twelve-week randomized trial in middle-aged and older adults found resistance training improved mitochondrial and strength measures, but nitrate-rich beetroot juice provided no additional benefit on molecular or functional outcomes.

Randomized double-blind pilot in women with type 2 diabetes found a green-coffee-extract plus magnesium-dimalate capsule regimen was feasible, but glycemic and cardiovascular biomarker effects were exploratory and inconclusive.

Triple-blind randomized trial in 60 primiparous postpartum women found fenugreek extract improved later PSQI sleep scores after baseline adjustment, but baseline sleep differed between groups and the study was small.

Randomized double-blind crossover trial in 38 adults dissatisfied with sleep found standardized Asparagus officinalis extract did not improve the primary N3-sleep endpoint but reduced wake after sleep onset and selected insomnia-symptom scores; subgroup findings were post hoc.

Small randomized double-blind crossover pharmacokinetic study in healthy adults characterized rapid absorption and urinary elimination of phenolics from a standardized propolis extract; evidence informs bioavailability rather than clinical efficacy.

Pilot randomized double-blind trial in 17 women with obesity found no between-group metabolic, inflammatory or iron-status differences surviving multiple-comparison correction after EGCG; metabolomic findings were nominal and exploratory.

Small randomized double-blind trial in adults with obesity found Moringa oleifera leaf extract reduced BMI and improved selected HbA1c, HDL, microbiome and metabolomic measures while preserving lean-mass-related measures; modest sample and multi-omic multiplicity require replication.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 70 women with low libido found standardized Shatavari root extract improved FSFI and several fatigue, sleep, anxiety and psychosocial scores over eight weeks; single-center proprietary-extract evidence requires independent replication.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 56 adults with uncomplicated URTI found a standardized andrographolide formulation improved symptom scores and mucus weight faster than placebo, while CRP and IL-8 changes were not clearly significant.

Multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial found standardized ginger extract reduced menstrual pain, dysmenorrhea severity, symptom burden and menstrual flow over three cycles, with favorable tolerability; formulation-specific replication remains important.

COSMOS-clinic ancillary analysis found neither a multivitamin-multimineral nor cocoa flavanol extract significantly changed two-year blood neurodegeneration biomarkers NfL, NT1 tau fragment or oligomeric amyloid-beta versus placebo.

Open-label randomized crossover trial in 31 mostly female young adults found eight weeks of walnut consumption modestly reduced total mood disturbance and increased urinary 5-HIAA and urolithins; small sample and open-label food intervention limit causal certainty.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 214 postmenopausal women found a standardized Asparagus racemosus extract improved several sexual-function and menopausal-symptom measures and oxidative-stress markers; proprietary formulation and broad endpoint set warrant independent replication.

Randomized crossover trial in 14 healthy normotensive postmenopausal women found short-term nitrate-rich beetroot juice did not alter blood-pressure or heart-rate reactivity to handgrip, post-exercise ischemia or cold pressor stress.

Eight-week randomized double-blind three-arm trial in 59 postmenopausal women found all gochujang formulations improved symptoms within groups, but there were no between-formulation differences and no placebo arm, so efficacy cannot be established.

Thirteen-year follow-up of a randomized prenatal vitamin D trial found no lasting benefit of higher-dose gestational vitamin D on offspring bone mineral content, bone density or fracture risk versus standard-dose supplementation.

Large COSMOS secondary analysis found daily multivitamin-multimineral supplementation did not reduce incident hypertension or two-year blood-pressure change overall; diet-quality and baseline-BP subgroup signals were exploratory and directionally inconsistent.

Systematic review of 43 clinical studies found the vitamin-E/cognition literature was dominated by dietary exposure and multivitamin studies, with very little isolated-supplement evidence; apparent protective associations may reflect dietary or multi-component synergy rather than vitamin E alone.

Four-week double-blind RCT in 155 adults with vitamin A, D or E deficiency found nutrition education plus multivitamin was not superior to nutrition education plus placebo for improving vitamin concentrations or deficiency rates; both groups improved substantially.

Two-year COSMOS biomarker substudy found multivitamin supplementation increased total carotenoids, lutein, beta-carotene and alpha-tocopherol concentrations, while several other carotenoids were unchanged; this demonstrates exposure/biomarker effects rather than clinical benefit.

Large COSMOS ancillary analysis found neither cocoa extract nor multivitamin-multimineral supplementation significantly reduced venous thromboembolism, DVT or pulmonary embolism in intention-to-treat analyses; per-protocol and latency patterns were exploratory.

Prespecified COSMOS ancillary study found small two-year changes favoring multivitamin supplementation on PCGrimAge and PCPhenoAge epigenetic clocks, while cocoa extract was null; effect sizes were small and clinical relevance remains uncertain.

COSMOS metabolomics substudy found nominal multivitamin-associated changes in DHA, omega-3, creatinine and multiple disease-risk scores, but none survived false-discovery-rate correction; findings are preliminary rather than validated metabolic benefits.

Twenty-four-week randomized prenatal trial found 6S-5-MTHF maintained total maternal/fetal folate similarly to folic acid while producing less detectable unmetabolized folic acid in maternal blood and placenta; clinical developmental superiority was not tested.

COSMOS clinic substudy found neither cocoa extract nor multivitamin supplementation improved two-year grip strength, walking speed, SPPB, balance, chair-stand or timed-up-and-go outcomes in older adults.

Single-blind randomized comparison found organically sourced and synthetic multivitamin-mineral formulations produced broadly comparable acute and 30-day circulating micronutrient profiles, providing no evidence of general bioavailability superiority for the organic formulation.

COSMOS secondary analysis found daily multivitamin supplementation did not significantly reduce COVID-19 incidence in intention-to-treat analysis; a symptomatic-COVID signal appeared only in adherent per-protocol analysis and remains secondary.

Twenty-four-week double-blind prenatal trial found a higher-biotin multivitamin increased maternal and cord-blood biotin biomarkers and reduced a marginal-insufficiency metabolite; cortisol associations were exploratory and no maternal or infant clinical benefit was established.

Exploratory systematic review/meta-analysis found highly heterogeneous psychiatric evidence for vitamin D and B12; vitamin-D signals attenuated toward null after bias adjustment and B12 supplementation evidence was sparse/null, supporting targeted deficiency assessment rather than routine supplementation.

Small double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 40 gynecologic-cancer patients found oral vitamin B12 reduced the incidence of questionnaire-defined chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, while neurotoxicity quality-of-life scores and adverse effects did not differ; replication is needed.

Tiny randomized crossover dental-surgery pilot replacing nighttime ibuprofen with melatonin, vitamin D and B12 did not improve overall recovery and produced higher pain/swelling on several measures; sex-interaction findings were exploratory and the multi-ingredient design prevents attribution.

Systematic review associated excessive folic-acid intake or high blood folate during preconception/pregnancy with gestational diabetes and selected offspring/growth outcomes, but evidence was heterogeneous and largely association-based; it does not establish a causal toxic threshold.

Randomized trial in 153 adults with B12-deficiency anemia found intranasal, intravenous and intramuscular B12 all produced short-term hematologic recovery, with no significant adjusted difference in hemoglobin response by route; some secondary laboratory kinetics differed.

Six-month double-blind community RCT in 472 Ethiopian teenage girls found B9/B12-fortified corn flour did not improve any primary cognitive outcome versus unfortified flour; a stunting-language interaction was secondary and not evidence of benefit.

One-month double-blind trial in a mostly female general-population sample found 100 mg/day vitamin B6 reduced depression scores only in preselected participants with elevated baseline symptoms, with no anxiety or stress benefit; subgroup design and high dose require cautious safety-aware interpretation.

Exploratory randomized rheumatology trial found increasing folic acid from 5 to 10 mg/week did not meaningfully reduce methotrexate-related liver or other toxicity over 12 weeks; a fatigue difference was isolated and secondary.

Randomized trial in 248 anemic children found adding Lactobacillus plantarum to iron-folic-acid therapy provided no additional benefit for hemoglobin, iron status, morbidity, adverse effects or gut-health markers versus iron-folic acid alone.

Large double-blind noninferiority trial in Bangladeshi women with iron-deficiency anemia found both tested bovine-lactoferrin doses were inferior to ferrous sulfate for 12-week hemoglobin recovery, with similar adverse-event rates.

Randomized pregnancy substudy in Ghana found multiple-micronutrient supplementation containing zinc did not significantly improve late-pregnancy plasma zinc or zinc-deficiency prevalence versus iron-folic acid; zinc status worsened across pregnancy in both groups.

Double-blind trial in couples with recurrent pregnancy loss found alpha-lipoic acid plus folic acid reduced sperm DNA-fragmentation index versus folic-acid control, while between-group sperm concentration, motility and morphology differences were not significant; fertility/live-birth benefit was not established.

Double-blind RCT in 110 pregnant women found equimolar 5-MTHF and folic acid produced comparable RBC-folate gains and homocysteine reductions; plasma 5-MTHF and unmetabolized-folate differences were borderline or nonsignificant after adjustment.
